rule_level_problems.problem: 'Shock' is used as a recorded finding but the page's definition of shock (footnote 1: SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) has no probable Shock rule, so the criterion only works if a clinician records shock by hand. SBP < 80 is covered separately; pulse, respiratory rate, restlessness and weakness are not.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable GORD in nausea/vomiting with dyspepsia
rule_level_problems.problem: Waist circumference threshold is sex-specific on the page (>= 80 cm woman, >= 94 cm man) and the rule uses 80 for all patients. Sex is not expressible in the language, so this should be recorded as a known approximation (over-calls GORD in men with waist 80-93 cm).

'Thirst due to water deprivation' is a narrow child concept; the page says 'thirst'. Descendants match but ancestors and siblings do not, so 'Thirst finding' (the general concept) would be the house-standard choice.
Fires for every adult with nausea or vomiting, including men; the language cannot restrict by sex. Acceptable as an 'exclude X' pre-screen, but worth noting.

The page says cholera is likely with watery diarrhoea 'with or without vomiting'; the rule additionally requires nausea or vomiting. On this page the patient has nausea/vomiting by definition, so the effect is nil here, but the rule would not help a diarrhoea-only presentation (presumably page 59 covers it).

rule_level_problems.rule: Measure BMI and waist circumference in dyspepsia with nausea/vomiting
rule_level_problems.problem: BMI is a routine vital (anchors/vitals.ts body_mass_index), so measuring it is redundant; waist circumference is the only non-routine measurement. Harmless.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: all fourteen criteria appear in the Urgent rule, the five 'X likely' conclusions (cholera, meningitis, peritonitis, appendicitis, pancreatitis) are probable rules referenced as active conditions, and anaphylaxis is a possible rule with every listed trigger. The most consequential gap is footnote 1's definition of shock, which is not encoded, so pulse >= 100, RR > 30, restlessness and weakness never make a patient urgent unless 'Shock' is recorded by hand. Below the box, gastroenteritis, dyspepsia, dehydration and pregnancy are encoded as the page intends; the GORD rule uses the woman's waist threshold (80 cm) for everyone because the language has no sex, and the dehydration rule's thirst concept is narrower than the page's 'thirst'.
